status: frozen before implementation and before observing any target-region-control result
motivation: The pre-registered full-frame foreground objective includes torso, clothing, and shoulders. Released queries may therefore trade supported head detail for non-head coverage. This control changes only the optimized target region.

intervention.head_roi: Convex hull of projected FLAME face, oral, eye, scalp, and ear vertices; neck excluded; 6-pixel dilation at 128x88.
intervention.rgb_and_alpha: Computed only inside the head envelope.
intervention.background_leak: Computed in a local exterior ring around the head envelope so silhouette leakage remains constrained without rewarding torso reconstruction.
intervention.validation_selection: Head-foreground MAE using the same envelope, rather than broad foreground MAE.
unchanged: NeRSemble nested identity sets and 20 official SVFR test identities
hidden dimension 128 and equal total parameter count
hard, adaptive-r150, and released-r150 G_mu interventions
ordinary and post-audit head-ROI evaluation metrics

primary_outcomes: head_foreground masked_psnr and lpips_alex_spatial at N_obs=4
head_supported masked_psnr and lpips_alex_spatial at N_obs=4
head_unsupported masked_psnr and lpips_alex_spatial at N_obs=4
mean query displacement and region-wise displacement
paired_inference: Average target cameras and training seeds within each held-out identity, then perform a 10,000-sample identity bootstrap.

predictions.allocation_confound_supported: Relative to the full-frame anchor, head-only training reduces released-query displacement toward neck/torso, improves released head-supported quality, and weakens the released advantage on torso without eliminating its head-unsupported scaling gain.
predictions.representation_bottleneck_supported: Even after head-only training, hard FLAME remains flat on head-unsupported content and the N_id=384 released-minus-hard head-unsupported advantage remains positive.
predictions.adaptive_release_supported: Adaptive release attains a better head-quality versus displacement frontier than either endpoint for at least one identity scale. This is not claimed in advance if the point is dominated.

falsifiers: If released head-unsupported gains vanish under head-only training, the main result was primarily a torso-target artifact rather than a head representation ceiling.
If released head-supported loss does not improve at all under head-only training, finite-budget allocation alone is insufficient to explain the supported-detail penalty.
If hard improves head-unsupported content with N_id under the head-only objective at the same rate as released, the claimed hard-support ceiling is falsified.
If adaptive points remain dominated across both identity scales, simple scalar release gating is not an effective APR mechanism.
disclosure: This control was designed after qualitative audit of the primary experiment and is labeled post-primary throughout. The original region analysis remains unchanged.
